source: docs/greater-anglia-d1/published-network.json (Nico oracle-clash-report, checked once against docs/london-se-national-rail-d1/published-network.json for the Liverpool Street stationGroup, 1 Sep 2026)
notes: National Rail (Darwin/OpenLDBWS) is structurally catalogued here but blocked at the account level — DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN not set. Same blocker as every other UK region packed so far.

Single primary agency (Greater Anglia). Thameslink/CrossCountry/East Midlands also call at Cambridge/Ely/Peterborough and pass the board-eligibility walk-up test alongside Greater Anglia — no doNotGroup needed at any Greater Anglia-owned station.

Hub lock Norwich (NRW). TWO secondary hubs, Cambridge (CBG) and Ipswich (IPS) — the oracle report gives both identical hub-tier language (report lines 22-24, 131), unlike West of England's single-secondary-hub shape. See hazard-pack.md H6.

Peterborough (PBO) is explicitly NOT a hub — flat throughRunningBoundary entry. LNER's board-eligibility verdict was undecided at D1 and resolved to `in` 5 Sep 2026 (unreserved coach always available, same evidence shape as West Yorkshire's LNER row at Leeds — see oracle-clash-report.md's Verdict resolution subsection) — the earlier `excludeOperators: ["LNER"]` boundary rested only on that open verdict and is removed now that it is resolved; LNER departures at Peterborough are on the board like every other in operator, confirmed live 5 Sep 2026 (docs/greater-anglia-d1/jim-handoff.md 'Adapter wired' section). East Midlands/Thameslink/CrossCountry are in.
Colchester (COL) and Ely (ELY) are kept flat under regional, not promoted to secondary-hub status, per the report's own third-tier/junction language (lines 37-38).

Liverpool Street is NOT included here — Greater Anglia services calling there are already documented as `in` in London & South East National Rail's built pack (docs/london-se-national-rail-d1/stations.json / stations.json, Liverpool Street (Greater Anglia) stationGroup, groupId liverpool-street, doNotGroup true). Not duplicated.

CRS collision caught, not propagated: the oracle report's own station-code list (line 103) assigns LST to Lowestoft, but LST is Liverpool Street's real-world CRS, already used in London & South East National Rail's built pack. Lowestoft never carries LST. All 14 CRS codes (including Lowestoft -> LWT) were verified live against Darwin on 5 Sep 2026 (scripts/fix-uk-region-crs.mjs greater-anglia --write; seven were wrong or missing in the original D1 pack — King's Lynn KLY->KLN, Thetford THF->TTF, Great Yarmouth YRD->GYM, Bishops Stortford BST->BIS, Diss/Wymondham/Lowestoft null->DIS/WMD/LWT) — every entry above now carries crsVerified: true.

Station scope is intentionally the ~13/14 stations the oracle report explicitly names, not the full 30-50 the report itself estimates for D1 — the remaining 16-36 stations are a flagged D2 gap (expand against the Transitland feed), not invented here.

Peterborough is flagged for a future multi-region ledger (cross-regional shared-platform de-dup with any East Midlands National Rail or LNER region Peterborough entry) — not resolved in this pack. This is a station-grouping question, separate from the LNER board-eligibility exclusion, which is resolved (see above).

Great Northern (Cambridge, King's Lynn, Ely) and CrossCountry (Stansted Airport) were discovered calling at these stations during 5 Sep 2026 live adapter wiring, beyond what the D1 station table itemised per station — both operators already carry a recorded `in` board-eligibility verdict elsewhere (Great Northern: this pack's own oracle line 91 Greater Thameslink Railway family + London & South East's oracle line 148; CrossCountry: this pack's own oracle, Peterborough/Ely Hereward Line corridor), so including them at these newly-observed stations is not a fresh unverified inclusion — same precedent as Thames Valley's CrossCountry-at-Oxford discovery. See docs/greater-anglia-d1/jim-handoff.md 'Adapter wired' section for the live evidence.

Nine Essex stations reassigned in from rest-of-england 15 Sep 2026 (docs/jim-brief-essex-to-greater-anglia.md, docs/uk-station-fill/assignment.md): Beaulieu Park, Burnham-on-Crouch, Chelmsford, Clacton-on-Sea, Harlow Mill, Harlow Town, Hatfield Peverel, Roydon, Southminster — resolving PR #399's Essex dual-claim between this pack and london-se-national-rail in Greater Anglia's favour (it operates every one of them: Great Eastern main line, Sunshine Coast and Crouch Valley branches, West Anglia line; already owns Colchester/Braintree/Witham on the same lines). CITY_BOUNDS's greater-anglia box (public/city-session.js) widened south (minLat 51.80 -> 51.64) to cover them; these nine are Darwin-verified from UK station fill phase 2a/2b, not this pack's original D1 pass, so they carry crsVerified/crsSource fields the rest of this catalog's original 14 stations do not need re-probing for. Now 130 stations.

stops.name: Norwich
stops.class: hub lock — single terminus, single operator (Greater Anglia), Great Eastern Main Line terminus, interchange for Norwich-Cambridge, Norwich-Great Yarmouth, Norwich-Lowestoft branches

stops.name: Cambridge
stops.class: secondary hub — Great Eastern Main Line interchange; Thameslink/Great Northern (Greater Thameslink Railway family) cross-London through-running passes the board-eligibility test alongside Greater Anglia, no separate boarding-area layer required. Great Northern confirmed live 5 Sep 2026 (printing 'Cambridge'/'London Kings Cross' at Cambridge itself, plus 'Kings Lynn'/'London Kings Cross' at King's Lynn and Ely) — same Greater Thameslink Railway family already `in` at Cambridge/Peterborough per this pack's own oracle report (line 91) and explicitly `in` in London & South East National Rail's oracle (line 148), not a fresh unverified operator.

stops.name: Ipswich
stops.class: secondary hub — major Great Eastern Main Line station, connections to London, Cambridge, Norwich, Peterborough; single operator

stops.name: Peterborough
stops.class: through-running/boundary point, explicitly NOT a merge or a hub (report line 25). LNER's board-eligibility verdict was undecided at D1, resolved to `in` 5 Sep 2026 (unreserved coach always available on a first-come-first-served basis, no compulsory reservation, no check-in barrier — same verdict and evidence shape as West Yorkshire's LNER row at Leeds; see oracle-clash-report.md's Verdict resolution subsection). The `excludeOperators` boundary that used to hide LNER here is removed — it rested only on the now-resolved undecided verdict, not on a stop-ownership reason; confirmed live 5 Sep 2026, LNER services to London Kings Cross, Edinburgh and Leeds appear on Peterborough's board (docs/greater-anglia-d1/jim-handoff.md 'Adapter wired' section). Still flagged for a multi-region ledger at D2 (cross-regional shared-platform de-dup with any East Midlands/LNER Peterborough entry) — that is a station-grouping question, not a board-eligibility one.

stops.name: Colchester
stops.class: regional hub (third tier) — Great Eastern Main Line, no through-running to adjacent regions except the already-documented Liverpool Street boundary

stops.name: Ely
stops.class: regional junction — Great Eastern Main Line (via Hereward Line) and Thameslink Cambridge branch meet here; Thameslink and CrossCountry pass the board-eligibility test

stops.name: King's Lynn
stops.class: branch terminus — West Anglia Main Line branch (Cambridge-King's Lynn). Great Northern confirmed live 5 Sep 2026 (prints 'Cambridge'/'London Kings Cross' at King's Lynn itself) — same Greater Thameslink Railway family already `in` per this pack's own oracle report line 91 and London & South East's oracle line 148.
